title: Binary Trees: Structure, Traversal, and Use Cases
description: Understand binary tree structures, common traversal methods, and practical applications.

flashcards.question: What is a binary tree?
flashcards.answer: A tree data structure where each node has at most two children, called left and right.

flashcards.question: What is the difference between a binary tree and a binary search tree?
flashcards.answer: A binary search tree (BST) maintains the property where left child nodes are less than the parent, and right child nodes are greater.

flashcards.question: Name the three common ways to traverse a binary tree.
In Inorder traversal, what is the order of visiting nodes?
Which traversal of a BST returns nodes in sorted order?
What is level-order traversal?
flashcards.answer: Visiting nodes level by level from top to bottom, left to right, usually implemented using a queue.

flashcards.question: What data structure is commonly used to implement level-order traversal?
What is the time complexity of traversing a binary tree?
flashcards.answer: O(n), where n is the number of nodes.

flashcards.question: How is the height of a binary tree defined?
flashcards.answer: The length of the longest path from the root node down to the farthest leaf node.

flashcards.question: What is a complete binary tree?
flashcards.answer: A binary tree where all levels are completely filled except possibly the last, which is filled from left to right.

flashcards.question: What is the difference between a full binary tree and a perfect binary tree?
flashcards.answer: A full binary tree has every node with either 0 or 2 children; a perfect binary tree is full and all leaves are at the same level.

flashcards.question: Why are binary trees useful in expression parsing?
flashcards.answer: They represent hierarchical expressions with operators as internal nodes and operands as leaves.

flashcards.question: How can you represent a binary tree in JavaScript?
flashcards.answer: Using objects with properties: `{ value, left, right }`.

flashcards.question: True or False: A binary tree can have cycles.
What is the main use case of a binary tree?
flashcards.answer: Hierarchical data representation, efficient searching, sorting, and expression parsing.
